newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dexia shares jump on takeover, results talk.
newsitem.headline: Dexia shares jump on takeover, results talk.

text.p: Shares in Franco-Belgian banking group Dexia jumped almost four percent on Monday after news it would make a major announcement this afternoon triggered market speculation of a takeover or buoyant 1996 results.

Dexia said chairman Pierre Richard would announce "an important financial operation," at the 1600 GMT news conference in Paris. The Belgian arm of Dexia said it would also hold a news conference at 1600 GMT in Brussels.
"Investors are speculating about a possible acquisition, with more people drawing a theoretical parallel between Fortis and Dexia," Kredietbank analyst Michel Ernst told Reuters.
He added that Belgo-Dutch bancassurance group Fortis has recently been "excessively dynamic and this success story could be the same for Dexia in coming years".
By 1405 GMT the share was up 3.1 percent at 3,470 francs, after touching a high of 3,510 francs, with over 220 million Belgian francs worth of the shares traded.
Bank analyst Stephane Roffler at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck said an acquisition could possibly involve a stake in a Dutch or Italian bank.
"Pierre Richard recently said he wanted to be present in Italy from 1997, maybe this (announcement) is an indication of this," Roffler said.

Talk focused on Crediop Spa, which like Dexia lends to public authorities, or alternatively on closer ties with Bank der Nederlandsche Gemeenten (BNG) of the Netherlands, which already has five percent in CLF-Dexia France, the French arm of the Franco-Belgian group.

The three groups are already in contact with each other as members Credit Local d'Europe, a group of seven banks specialising in lending to public authorities. Its other members, Deutsche Girozentrale-Deutsche Kommunalbank of Germany, Banco de Credito Local de Espana, Caixa Goral de Depositos of Portugal, are seen as less likely targets.
Mignon's Roffler noted the Dexia share was not very expensive. This could be another explanation for the price rise.
"An alliance with an Italian bank or a Dutch one has been circulating in the market," said one trader at a major Belgian bank. Dexia gave no further details on today's announcement.
Analysts expected 1996 profits to be strong.
Dexia chairman Richard has said he expected combined 1997 profit in excess of three billion French francs.
"Regarding profitability we've seen that 1996 has been a good year for Dexia," said Michel Ernst. "In the coming years Dexia will continue to grow through internal and external growth."
